title: Pace Prints Buys Brand X, Becoming One of the Largest Printmakers in the US
summary: Pace Prints today announced that it has purchased publisher Brand X Editions. In acquiring the Long Island, New York–based workshop, with which it has long collaborated, Pace has become one of the largest printmakers in the United States. The two workshops will maintain their operations, while Pace Prints will expand into Los Angeles as well. […]

title: Peter Max, Icon of Psychedelic Art, Dies at 88
summary: Peter Max, whose trippy Day-Glo paintings came to symbolize the Flower Power era of the 1960s, died on September 18 in a hospital in New York at the age of eighty-eight. title: Centre for Contemporary Arts Tashkent Opens in Uzbekistan
summary: The Centre for Contemporary Arts Tashkent (CCA Tashkent), Uzbekistan’s first permanent institution devoted to contemporary art, opened to the public on September 6. London-born curator, writer, and educator Sara Raza was named artistic director and chief curator last year. title: Renoir Show Breaks Box-Office Record at London’s National Gallery
summary: Ticket sales for the National Gallery’s forthcoming Renoir exhibition have topped twenty-two thousand, setting a record for the London institution. Bookings opened to members on August 4, and to the general public on August 25. title: The Met Breaks Ground on New Modern and Contemporary Wing
summary: On September 15, the Metropolitan Museum of Art broke ground on the Oscar L. Tang and H.M. Agnes Hsu-Tang Wing, a long-awaited addition that will house the museum’s collection of modern and contemporary art. The new wing is scheduled to open to the public in 2030. title: Andrei Rublev Icon Warped After Climate-Control Failure
summary: The prized Russian icon Trinity, painted by Andrei Rublev in the fifteenth-century, has possibly been damaged after the climate-control system in which the work is housed broke down. The icon is currently kept in the Trinity-St. Sergius Lavra monastery near Moscow, a Unesco World Heritage site. The work was transferred to the Russian Orthodox Church […]

title: Pem Lham Wins $30k Rubin Museum Himalayan Art Prize
summary: The Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art has named Bhutanese mixed-media artist Pem Lham the winner of the 2026 Rubin Museum Himalayan Art Prize. The honor is presented annually to a contemporary artist from the Himalayan region. It is attended by a $30,000 cash award, making it the largest prize of its kind in the world. […]
